pick.headline: Vance and Owen put their peace plan for Bosnia on the table
pick.summary: On January 2, 1993, at talks in Geneva, the cochairmen of the international conference on the former Yugoslavia, Cyrus Vance for the UN and Lord Owen for the European Community, presented the leaders of Bosnia's three warring sides with a plan dividing the republic into ten largely autonomous provinces.
pick.significance: The Vance-Owen plan was the main international attempt to end the Bosnian war in 1993. The new Clinton administration was cool toward it, the Bosnian Serb assembly rejected it in May, and the war went on until Dayton in 1995.
pick.fbis: The East Europe report of January 4, 1993, carried TANJUG from Geneva: the three Bosnian leaders were shown two maps, the one Vance and Owen had presented the day before and a rival from Izetbegovic, and the Croat leader Mate Boban objected from the start.
